title: private-deployments-weekly-2026-04-27
content:
Private Deployments - Weekly Update (2026-04-27)

Summary:
- Focus this week: unblock two priority customer installs (Acme Health VPC peering, FinSolve on-prem installer), stabilize cert rotation flow for Private control plane, and ship small improvements to the on-prem installer to reduce manual steps.
- Status: Acme Health largely unblocked pending final network validation; FinSolve remains blocked on post-install service start failures.

Standup highlights (daily quick notes):
- Mon 04/20: Kickoff incident triage for Acme Health; reproduced VPC peering asymmetry in staging; created JIRA-PD-78. Started work on automating route validation checks.
- Tue 04/21: Jonah debugged control-plane auth failures during acme peering test — found MTU mismatch on provider NAT. Opened MR to add MTU check to preflight.
- Wed 04/22: Sofia reproduced FinSolve failure on Ubuntu 22.04 VM image: systemd unit for redwood-service was failing due to race with init script that writes config (timing issue).
- Thu 04/23: Deployed installer fix (gitlab MR 512) to staging that adds explicit systemd unit start-after and healthcheck loop; initial tests looked promising but one customer environment still hit startup timeout.
- Fri 04/24: Ran joint run with FinSolve site ops; captured detailed logs (attached in slack thread). We discovered the customer has a custom PAM module that delays system boot which pushes the installer into a timeout window.

Customer escalations / blockers:
1) Acme Health (priority P1) - VPC peering & route propagation
   - Symptom: Intermittent failures between customer-hosted app and private-control-plane endpoints after peering established.
   - Root cause hypothesis: MTU fragmentation on provider-managed NAT + delayed BGP route advertisement causing TCP resets for larger payloads.
   - Work this week: Added an MTU validation step to the VPC preflight and a recommended route advertise check script. Deployed an interim customer-side workaround (force MTU=1400) which stabilized their traffic in staging.
   - Remaining work: Coordinate with customer network team to roll MTU change in production, confirm BGP stability window with provider. Owner: Liam O'Connor. ETA: 2026-04-30.
   - Jira: JIRA-PD-78 (networking)

2) FinSolve (priority P1) - On-prem installer: redwood-service fails to start
   - Symptom: Installer completes but redwood-service systemd unit fails with TimeoutStartSec, then enters crash loop when manually started.
   - Root cause hypothesis: Installer assumes systemd is ready and that config files are immediately available; customer VM uses a slow init path and custom PAM module delaying readiness.
   - Work this week: Deployed MR 512 with retries/healthcheck; added jittered exponential backoff to service-start step; captured extended logs during joint run.
   - Remaining work: Add a patient installer mode (longer timeouts + optional manual-confirm flow) and document known problematic init environments in the runbook. Owner: Sofia Martinez. ETA: 2026-05-05.
   - Linked items: gitlab.com/redwood/infrastructure/merge_requests/512

Control plane cert rotation 
- Observed: Two customers reported 401s during automated cert rotation window (both on private deployments using managed KMS integration).
- Root cause: Rotation job started earlier than scheduled on the control plane due to timezone parsing bug in cron wrapper; new certs not yet propagated to all control plane replicas before rotation.
- Mitigation: Rolled back auto-rotation and patched cron wrapper to canonicalize timezone parsing. Patch merged and staged (CONFLUENCE-priv-deploys-runbook documents the change). Owner: Jonah Park. ETA to redeploy: 2026-04-29.

Work in progress / engineering tasks:
- Installer updates: MR 512 (systemd start ordering + retry loop) in staging. Next: patient mode toggle and clearer logs.
- VPC preflight tool: add MTU & BGP propagation validation; prototype script in /tmp on staging; wrap into installer preflight next week. Owner: Liam.
- Runbook updates: Documented known init/systemd pitfalls and customer-facing troubleshooting steps. Draft POC page in Confluence; reviewers: Aisha, Sofia.
- Telemetry: Add additional startup traces for on-prem installs to correlate installer phases with systemd boot timestamps. Owner: Jonah.

Decisions made:
- Short-term: Ship MR 512 + patient mode as optional flag rather than default to avoid regressions for fast-boot environments.
- Medium-term: Add explicit preflight checks for common cloud vendor quirks (MTU, custom init delays) and surface results on the plan page before installs.

Risks / open questions:
- Some customers cannot change MTU (managed hardware) — need fallback options (e.g., enable TCP MSS clamping on gateway). Need networking team input.
- Patient mode increases installer duration and could impact automated provisioning pipelines; need to work with customer SREs to offer an opt-in install profile.

Action items (owner, due):
- Liam O'Connor: Finalize MTU/BGP preflight script and provide customer run instructions (due 2026-04-30).
- Sofia Martinez: Implement patient-mode flag in the installer and publish updated runbook section (due 2026-05-05).
- Jonah Park: Redeploy patched cert-rotation cron wrapper to staging and validate end-to-end rotation window (due 2026-04-29).
- Aisha Khan: Coordinate sync with networking team and Acme Health; schedule joint call if provider cannot commit to route stability (due 2026-04-28).

Notes / attachments:
- Logs and test capture: slack:#pd-ops thread 04/23 (FinSolve joint run)
- MR: gitlab.com/redwood/infrastructure/merge_requests/512 (installer systemd retry)
- Jira: JIRA-PD-78 (Acme network)
- Draft runbook: CONFLUENCE-priv-deploys-runbook

Meeting notes (2026-04-24 post-mortem sync):
- Attendees: Aisha, Liam, Sofia, Jonah, FinSolve eng lead (Erin), Acme netops (Sam).
- Key takeaway: Two distinct classes of failure (network-level MTU/BGP timing vs host-level init delays). Both are addressable but require different mitigations and customer coordination.
- Action: prioritize quick preflight checks and offer an explicit opt-in patient install profile.

Next week plan (2026-04-27 -> 2026-05-03):
- Finish MTU preflight and roll instruction to Acme; confirm production stabilization.
- Ship patient-mode flag behind feature flag; run additional tests on slow-boot images.
- Validate cert rotation fix in staging and schedule a controlled rotation window with one pilot customer.
- Continue collecting installer telemetry and add a transient debug flag that can be toggled for a single install to capture prolonged logs without increasing default verbosity.

Questions for leadership / blockers requiring cross-team help:
- Do we have bandwidth from networking domain experts to propose gateway-level MSS clamping as a fallback? (need contact)
- Legal / compliance: any constraints on recommending customer-side MTU changes for regulated customers? (flagged for CS)

Status summary (one-line): In-progress — Acme largely stabilized with MTU workaround; FinSolve blocked by slow init path, patient-mode + runbook changes expected to unblock within two sprints.

Prepared by: Aisha Khan (eng-private-deployments)
